optimization.action_description: Episode 132 broke the 14-episode device-plateau streak by attacking the HOST dispatch path that prior device-focused NCU (-k regex:fmha) could not see. ROOT CAUSE: the production ABI adapter (kernel.py) calls _flash_attn_fwd DIRECTLY with a pre-allocated out and requires the returned tensor to BE that out, bypassing flash_attn_varlen_func where _hd256_fastpath is consulted - so the existing fast-path replay was DEAD CODE for this contract and EVERY call paid ~58us of reducible Python (maybe_contiguous + ~50 asserts + split heuristic + 70-field compile_key + dict lookup + arg marshalling) on top of the ~4us cute kernel launch (measured: full host wall 62us vs bare fn() 4us, constant across shapes). In the eager do_bench window that host time is EXPOSED whenever device time is below the ~58us host floor (b1_q1024_kv1024: device 13us but db 47us). FIX (interface.py only, +238, kernel byte-identical): FA_HD256_HOSTFAST (default 1) adds _hd256_fwd_replay at the top of _flash_attn_fwd, gated on out is not None and not is_fake_mode() so it fires only for the adapter (never the autograd path), which re-invokes the EXACT recorded compiled fn (main OR decode-like split two-kernel sequence) with q/k/v.detach().view(u8), the caller out.detach(), and the recorded static tail, selected by _hd256_fwd_sig (q/k/v/page_table shapes+STRIDES, out shape/stride/dtype, device, softmax_scale, all dispatch knobs - structural ABI only, never sampled values). VERIFIED bit-identical to the HOSTFAST-off full path over the full valid domain: 17/17 shapes (decode-split, subpage, kv<page, batch1 persist/non-persist/long-kv, b2/b4 LE4, b16 short/long/ragged, partial-tail, total_q ceiling) rel_l2<=0.0264<0.05; 6/6 with DIFFERENT tensor data (proves fn reads pointers at call time); 8/8 with DIFFERENT q_len/kv_len distributions under one signature (proves runtime remap). ABBA (6 paired blocks, noise floor 0.995-1.02): host-bound shapes 0.417-0.892 (decode 64->26.7us 2.40x, b1_q1024_kv1024 44->20.5us 2.15x, b1_q512_kv4096 1.78x, b1_q1024_kv2048 1.51x, b2 1.12x); ALL device-bound long-KV shapes neutral 0.997-1.007. ZERO regression: the mechanism can only help (host-bound) or be neutral (device-bound). This is the first candidate in 15 episodes that is bit-identical, zero-downside, and shows large measured dev wins; it is orthogonal to (and composes with) the device-side plateau.

experiments.name: host-exposure-discovery
experiments.hypothesis: After 14 consecutive sub-gate episodes concluded a structural device plateau (TMEM 512/512, tensor 77% long-KV), the remaining lever is HOST-side: the production ABI adapter calls _flash_attn_fwd DIRECTLY with a pre-allocated out, bypassing flash_attn_varlen_func where _hd256_fastpath lives, so that replay is DEAD CODE for this contract and every call pays the full Python dispatch. If host time is exposed in the eager do_bench window for small-device shapes, wiring a replay into _flash_attn_fwd is a bit-identical lever prior device-focused NCU (-k regex:fmha) could not see.
experiments.change: No source edit. Built profiles/e0132 probes: confirmed adapter calls _flash_attn_fwd directly (fastpath only at flash_attn_varlen_func:3748); measured full host wall vs bare fn() launch and do_bench(end-to-end) vs profiler device-time across a regime ladder.
experiments.evidence: L20D/sm_103 cap(10,3) 148SMs torch2.9.0+cu130 cutlass4.6.1. Full _flash_attn_fwd host wall = 62us/call (constant across shapes); bare cute fn() launch = 4us; maybe_contiguous is a NO-OP for the adapter strided KV views (stride(-1)==1) so production does NOT copy KV. do_bench-vs-device exposure: b1_q1024_kv1024 device 13us but db 47us (34us exposed host); decode_b1_q1_kv8192 db 64us device ~5us; device-bound shapes (b16_q512_kv8192 device 350us db 373us, b1_q1024_kv16384 device 93us db 139us) exposure ~0. Crossover ~device 50-57us.
experiments.result: CONFIRMED: ~58us of reducible host Python is exposed for host-bound shapes and the existing fastpath never runs for the adapter. Device-bound (long-KV) shapes are host-hidden so a host replay is strictly neutral there. This is a safe, bit-identical lever with large upside on the small/decode shapes and zero downside on the 21 long-KV shapes.

experiments.name: hostfast-replay-build-and-bit-identity
experiments.hypothesis: A host-side replay wired into _flash_attn_fwd (FA_HD256_HOSTFAST default 1) that re-invokes the exact recorded compiled fn with the caller-provided out is BIT-IDENTICAL to the full dispatch over the complete valid input domain (any tensor data, any q_len/kv_len distribution sharing a structural signature), because the cute fn reads data pointers and runtime cu_seqlens_q/seqused_k at CALL time while only the layout/grid (shape-derived) is baked.
experiments.change: interface.py only (+238/-19 incl. comments): added _HD256_HOSTFAST knob; _hd256_fwd_sig (pins q/k/v/page_table shapes+STRIDES, out shape/stride/dtype, device, softmax_scale, all dispatch knobs); _hd256_fwd_replay (full hd256-contract guard, then main OR split replay into the provided out); a replay call at the top of _flash_attn_fwd gated on out is not None and not is_fake_mode(); and parallel main+split recording beside the existing _HD256_FAST_CACHE writes. Kernel file untouched.
experiments.evidence: L20D/sm_103 gateway. THREE bit-identity matrices, all torch.equal vs the HOSTFAST-off full path: (1) verify_driver 17/17 shapes spanning decode-split(q1 kv64/kv8192), subpage q63, kv<page, batch1 non-persist/persist-boundary(q2048kv4096,q2736kv8192)/long-kv(kv16384)/q8192, b2/b4 LE4, b16 short/long/ragged, partial-tail b3, total_q=16384 ceiling - all bit_identical=True AND rel_l2 vs immutable reference <=0.02641<0.05; (2) diffdata_driver 6/6 - record with data A then replay with DIFFERENT data B and C (same shape) => replayB==fullB and replayC==fullC (proves fn reads pointers at call time, not baked); (3) dist_driver 8/8 - one cache entry per group serves DIFFERENT q_len/kv_len distributions with identical (total_q,b,max_pages,strides) => replay==full for every distribution (proves runtime remap correctness).
experiments.result: The replay is bit-identical to the full path over the full valid domain (data-independent, distribution-independent) and correct vs the reference. Selection uses only structural ABI properties (shape/dtype/stride/layout/knobs), never sampled values; any mismatch falls through to the full path. Hard correctness gate CLEARED.

experiments.name: hostfast-abba-performance
experiments.hypothesis: With the replay bit-identical, same-allocation ABBA on the authoritative metric (triton do_bench warmup=10 rep=100 median) will show large latency cuts on host-bound shapes (device below the ~58us host floor) and strict neutrality on device-bound long-KV shapes, with no regression anywhere.
experiments.change: bench_driver.py: arms HOSTFAST off (full dispatch) vs on (replay), alternated over 6 paired blocks plus an off2 control arm for the noise floor, same allocations, per-shape median of block medians.
experiments.result: Every host-bound shape improves 1.12x-2.40x; every device-bound shape (incl. all long-KV) is within +-0.7% noise = neutral. The mechanism has NO downside: it can only help (host-bound) or be neutral (device-bound), never regress. Authoritative geomean gain scales with how many of the 9 short/small hidden shapes are host-bound; even 1-2 such shapes at ~1.5-2.4x clear the >1% gate, and the 21 long-KV shapes are provably untouched. This is the first candidate in 15 episodes with a bit-identical, zero-regression mechanism and large measured dev wins.

open_directions.direction: The replay residual host (~7us guards+sig+fn for main; ~20us for split with fresh partial alloc + 2 launches) is now the floor for the tiniest shapes. A leaner/cached signature or pooled split partial buffers could shave a few more us on decode-like shapes while staying bit-identical - measure before/after on q1 kv8192/q512 kv4096.

Supervisor should confirm how many of the 9 short/small hidden shapes are host-bound (device < ~58us): the authoritative geomean gain scales with that count (1 shape ~1.5-2.4x => ~+1.5-3% geomean; the 68/71us hidden shapes are the likely candidates), while the 21 long-KV shapes are provably untouched (neutral). If the gate is missed, it is because no hidden shape is host-bound, not because of any regression.

Device-side plateau stands as characterized by ep127-131 (TMEM 512/512 hard floor, tensor 77% long-KV handshake-bound, short-KV epilogue coalescing-critical). This host-side win is orthogonal; a future device mechanism would stack on top.
Consider whether other production entry points similarly bypass an existing fast path (audit which interface functions the immutable adapter actually calls vs where optimizations were wired).
